item.title: City complete signing of Guehi
item.description: Manchester City have completed the signing of Marc Guehi from Crystal Palace. The England defender has signed a five-and-a-half year contract with the transfer deal costing 20-million pounds. Guehi captained Palace to FA Cup success last season and is City's second January transfer after Antoine Semenyo's move from Bournemouth. Advertisement

item.title: Rás Mumhan retains four‑day five‑stage format
item.description: Dornan Rás Mumhan this year retains its established four‑day, five‑stage format. Stage 1 on Friday April 3rd is a team time trial from Ballybunion to Asdee. That afternoon takes the riders from Asdee to Knockanure. Saturday is from Killarney to Portmagee, Sunday goes from Millstreet to Clondrohid and the Killorglin finale takes place on the Monday. item.description: Things haven’t gone quite the way of trainer Gordon Elliott’s into the New Year as it had over Christmas, but the Cullentra handler snapped a frustrating run of outs when Needs Must won the maiden hurdle at Fairyhouse last Thursday by over three lengths at odds of 15-8 second favourite. item.title: Killester win WSL National Cup
item.description: Killester won their fifth Domino’s WSL National Cup, defeating FloMAX Liffey Celtics 70-64, avenging last season’s defeat in the final to the same opponents. Samantha Haiby picked up the MVP with 30 points, followed closely by 20-point performance from Killester captain Michelle Clarke. Clarke certainly led by example in the opening minutes, landing two three’s, as she grabbed eight of Killester’s opening 11 points, to help the Dublin side into an early 11-7 lead. item.title: New National Historic Rally Championship to be in included Triton Showers-backed series
item.description: A new National Historic Rally Championship is set to be incorporated into the Triton Showers Motorsport Ireland National Rally Championship for the 2026 season. This marks the first time that a dedicated national title for historic machinery will be contested within the framework of the main national series. item.title: The Humanity Ball in Tralee raises over €245,000 for charities
item.description: The Humanity Ball, a New Year’s Eve black-tie event in Tralee, has raised €245, 329 for three charities. The event, which took place in Ballygarry Estate Hotel and Spa, was a fundraiser for Kerry Hospice Foundation, One4Humanity and the Tír na nÓg Chidren’s Foundation. Cheques were presented today at the Ballygarry venue. Advertisement Kerry Hospice Foundation received over €165,000. Jenny Tarrant from Kerry Hospice thanked The Humanity Ball organisers and everyone who donated to the event. Adve

item.title: Kerry councillors back motion of no confidence in the Road Safety Authority
item.description: Councillors in Kerry have backed a motion of no confidence in the Road Safety Authority. It follows a motion tabled by independent councillor Jackie Healy-Rae at today’s full council meeting. He urged members write to the Transport Minister expressing no confidence in the RSA in its current format, and urged a re-evaluation of its role. item.title: Kerry sides set to contest All-Ireland Schools Cup finals
item.description: 2 Kerry sides will tomorrow contest All-Ireland Schools Cup finals at the National Arena in Dublin. Both are from Castleisland Community College, who play in the U16 Girls and Boys "A" deciders. The girls face Presentation Kilkenny @ 12.30, the boys St Pats Cavan from 2.
